dishes.name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Garlic Potatoes & Carrots
dishes.why: Cheap chicken thighs paired with affordable potatoes and carrots make a hearty, budget‑friendly dinner.

dishes.name: Pan‑Seared Pork Chops with Broccoli & Mushrooms
dishes.why: Tender pork chops get flavor from butter‑garlic and are complemented by broccoli and mushrooms.

dishes.name: Ground Beef Stir‑Fry over Rice
dishes.why: Versatile ground beef cooked with soy sauce and served over fluffy rice is quick and cheap.

dishes.name: Shrimp Pasta with Mushroom Tomato Sauce
dishes.why: Shrimp adds protein to a simple pasta tossed with mushroom‑tomato sauce.

dishes.name: Pan‑Roasted Salmon with Sweet Potato Cubes
dishes.why: Salmon pairs nicely with caramelized sweet potatoes for a nutritious, low‑carb dinner.

plan.notes: All five meals use the best‑priced proteins and pair them with on‑sale vegetables or pantry staples, while the stock‑up list captures versatile items (rice, pasta, sauce, canned tuna, oatmeal) for future weeks.

transcript.content:
You are a home cook planning a week of meals from this week's grocery flyers near the user.
You cannot see the flyers directly: browse them with the tools. Start with list_deal_types, then
open the categories you need. Plan the way an experienced bargain-hunting cook does:
1. Find the anchors: the genuinely good protein and main-component deals worth building meals around
   (compare the same item across stores).
2. Find discounted pantry staples worth stocking up on.
3. Pair each anchor with sensible sides that are also on sale.
Only real meals from real cooking ingredients. You have at most 15 tool calls; when you have
enough, stop calling tools and reply with the final plan.

**User requirements:**
- Household: 2 people
- Plan: 5 dinners
- Pantry the user already has (use freely, cost $0): salt, black pepper, vegetable oil, olive oil, butter, all-purpose flour, sugar, garlic, yellow onion, dried oregano, dried basil, paprika, ground cumin, chili flakes, soy sauce, vinegar, dijon mustard, chicken or vegetable stock, rice, eggs

Return ONLY a JSON object of this shape (no comments, no code fences):
{
  "dishes": [
    {
      "name": "Roast chicken with garlic potatoes",
      "anchor_deal_ids": [123],
      "side_deal_ids": [456, 789],
      "pantry_items": ["salt", "olive oil"],
      "why": "one sentence"
    }
  ],
  "stock_up_deal_ids": [321],
  "notes": "one or two sentences on the overall plan"
}
Field meanings: anchor_deal_ids = the main component(s) the dish is built around; side_deal_ids =
sides and supporting ingredients bought this week; pantry_items = ONLY items from the user's pantry
list; stock_up_deal_ids = discounted staples worth buying extra of for future weeks.
Rules: exactly 5 dishes. Every deal id must be copied from the deals you were shown -- never
invent one. A deal bought once may be used in several dishes. Build every dish from real cooking
ingredients on sale.
